text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Monday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Chairman of the Centre Union Board Egidijus Bichkauskas said that Kestutis Glaveckas, vice chairman of parliament's finance and budget committee, would be the "most acceptable" prime minister for Lithuania. The Centre Union will meet at the end of June to decide whether to form a shadow government.
- For the first time in Lithuanian basketball history, the women's national team became the European champions. The Lithuanian women's team beat Slovakia 72:62 in Budapest Sunday.

- According to Banque Paribas experts, Lithuanian Telecom's value could be between 1.6 billion litas and 3.2 billion litas. The paper says that Lithuanian experts see Banque Paribas as one of the most serious candidates for adviser in the privatisation of Lithuanian Telecom. Banque Paribas representative Richard Goldman said his bank's proposal was to privatise Lithuanian Telecom in two stages. The first would be to sell a large package of shares to a strategic investor. Then, six months to one year later, to sell to international investors.

- Supreme electoral commission chairman Zenonas Vaigauskas said that Lithuanian law does not recognise Lithuanian-American Valdas Adamkus as permanently living in Lithuania. The supreme electoral commission doubts whether Adamkus can be registered as a candidate for the post of Lithuanian president.

- Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius criticised a statement by Estonian Prime Minister Mart Siimann. "Estonian Prime Minister Mart Siiman was probably mistaken declaring that future European Union members will be evaluated according to their geopolitical situation," the paper said, quoting a statement distributed by Vagnorius's office Friday.

- At the end of July or in August, a package of Utenos Beverages shares could be sold to either Baltic Beverages Holdings or Carlsberg. According to Stasys Poshkus, director of Valeksa, a consultancy specialising in breweries, representatives of the agricultural ministry who manage the state's shares in Utenos have already agreed during a shareholders meeting to present BBH and Carlsberg investment projects.

- The central bank reminded Tauro Bank shareholders, council and administration that they will be held accountable if they do not act according to the law. The board of Tauro Bank, which was suspended by the central bank last week, accused the Bank of Lithuania of making "chaos."

- The chairman of the Lithuanian Savings Bank's board, Vygintas Bubnys, presented his resignation last week, following a declaration by Lithuanian Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta that the bank's board needed to be changed.
